children.name: Chaetorhynchus
children.description: Chaetorhynchus — a genus of drongos in the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Chaetorhynchus papuensis
children.description: The drongo fantail, also known as the pygmy drongo, is a species of passerine bird endemic to the island of New Guinea. It is the only species in the genus Chaetorhynchus. The species was long placed within the drongo family Dicruridae, but it differs from others in that family in having twelve rectrices instead of ten.

children.name: Dicrurus
children.description: The typical drongos — a genus of medium-sized, entirely black or dark grey passerines with deeply forked tails, found across Africa, Asia, and Australasia. They are aggressive, fearless birds that will attack much larger species that approach their nests, including raptors and crows. They are accomplished aerial insectivores and noted vocal mimics, incorporating the calls of other birds into their own repertoire.

children.name: Dicrurus admirabilis
children.description: A drongo endemic to Sulawesi, Indonesia.

children.name: Dicrurus adsimilis
children.description:
The fork-tailed drongo (Dicrurus adsimilis), also called the common drongo or African drongo, is a small bird found from the Sahel to South Africa that lives in wooded habitats, particularly woodlands and savannas. It is part of the family Dicruridae and has four recognized subspecies, D. A adsimilis, D. A. Apivorus, D. A. Fugax and D. A. Jubaensis. Like other drongos, the fork-tailed is mostly insectivorous; its diet mainly consists of butterflies, termites, and grasshoppers.
Physically, this species is characterized with a narrow fork-shaped tail, red-brownish eyes, and black plumage throughout all of its body. These birds nest close to wetlands, forests, and farms and the breeding season varies depending the region. The female usually lays one to four eggs, which hatch in 15 to 18 days.

children.name: Dicrurus aeneus
children.description: The bronzed drongo (Dicrurus aeneus) is a small Indomalayan bird belonging to the drongo group.

children.name: Dicrurus aldabranus
children.description: The Aldabra drongo is a species of bird in the drongo family Dicruridae. It is endemic to Seychelles, where it occurs only on the island of Aldabra. It has a small population of only around 1000 birds.

children.name: Dicrurus alternans
children.description: A drongo endemic to the Philippines.

children.name: Dicrurus andamanensis
children.description: The Andaman Drongo (Dicrurus andamanensis) is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus annectans
children.description: The crow-billed drongo (Dicrurus annectens) is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae. It is native to moist tropical forests of southeastern Asia where its range extends from India to the Philippines and Indonesia. It is a completely black bird with a shallowly forked tail and is similar in appearance to the black drongo. It breeds between April and June, the cup-shaped nest being built in the fork of a branch by both birds, the female afterwards incubating the eggs. It is a common bird and the IUCN has listed it as "least concern".

children.name: Dicrurus atripennis
children.description: The shining drongo (Dicrurus atripennis) is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus balicassius
children.description: The balicassiao (Dicrurus balicassius) is a species of passerine bird in the family Dicruridae. It is endemic to the Philippines. Its natural habitat is tropical moist lowland forests.

children.name: Dicrurus bracteatus
children.description: The spangled drongo (Dicrurus bracteatus) is a bird of the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus caerulescens
children.description: The white-bellied drongo (Dicrurus caerulescens) is a species of drongo found across the Indian Subcontinent. Like other members of the family Dicruridae, they are insectivorous and mainly black in colour, but with a white belly and vent. Young birds are, however, all black and may be confused with the black drongo, which is smaller and more compact in appearance. The subspecies found in Sri Lanka has white restricted to the vent.

children.name: Dicrurus forficatus
children.description: The crested drongo (Dicrurus forficatus) is a passerine bird in the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus fuscipennis
children.description: The Grand Comore drongo is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae. It is endemic to Comoros.

children.name: Dicrurus grandis
children.description: A large drongo endemic to the Philippines.

children.name: Dicrurus hottentottus
children.description:
The hair-crested drongo (Dicrurus hottentottus) is an Asian bird of the family Dicruridae. This species was formerly considered conspecific with Dicrurus bracteatus, for which the name "spangled drongo" - formerly used for both - is now usually reserved. Some authorities include the Sumatran drongo (D. Sumatranus) in D. Hottentottus as subspecies.
It is native from Pakistan, Bangladesh, India, and Bhutan through Indochina to China, Indonesia, and Brunei. Hair-crested drongos move in small flocks and are very noisy. The "spangled drongo", Dicrurus bracteatus, is native on the east coast of Australia and its name is pejorative slang for a silly person. This may be due to its strange chattering and cackling.

children.name: Dicrurus leucophaeus
children.description: The ashy drongo (Dicrurus leucophaeus) is a species of bird in the drongo family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus ludwigii
children.description:
The square-tailed drongo (Dicrurus ludwigii), formerly the common square-tailed drongo, is a passerine bird in the family Dicruridae. It is a common resident breeder in parts of southern Africa.
These insectivorous birds are usually found in forests or dense bush. They are aggressive and fearless birds, given their small size, and will attack much larger species if their nest or young are threatened. The male is mainly glossy black, although the wings are duller. The female is similar but less glossy. The bill is black and heavy, and the eye is red. This species is similar to the fork-tailed drongo, but is smaller, and the shorter tail lacks the deep fork which gives the latter species its name. The fork-tailed drongo is also typically found in more open habitat. The common square-tailed drongo has short legs and sits very upright whilst perched prominently, like a shrike. It flycatches or take prey from the ground. The call is a harsh. Two to three eggs are laid in a cup nest in a fork high in a tree.

children.name: Dicrurus macrocercus
children.description: The black drongo (Dicrurus macrocercus) is a small Asian passerine bird of the drongo family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus megarhynchus
children.description: The paradise drongo or ribbon-tailed drongo (Dicrurus megarhynchus) is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus menagei
children.description: The Tablas drongo (Dicrurus menagei) is an Asian bird of the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus modestus
children.description: The velvet-mantled drongo (Dicrurus modestus) is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae. It is found throughout the Cameroon line and the African tropical rainforest.

children.name: Dicrurus montanus
children.description: The Sulawesi drongo (Dicrurus montanus) is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus mycterians
children.description: A glossy black drongo with deeply forked tail, found across South and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Dicrurus paradiseus
children.description: The greater racket-tailed drongo (Dicrurus paradiseus) is a medium-sized Asian bird which is distinctive in having elongated outer tail feathers with webbing restricted to the tips.

children.name: Dicrurus remifer
children.description:
The lesser racket-tailed drongo (Dicrurus remifer) is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae. It is found in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.
It is found in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia, ranging across Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, and Vietnam. Its natural habitat is near the edge or inside of subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Dicrurus sumatranus
children.description: The Sumatran drongo (Dicrurus sumatranus) is a passerine bird in the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Dicrurus waldeni
children.description: A drongo endemic to Mayotte in the Comoros Islands.
